candidate.answerReason: The distance increases sixfold and the speed increases threefold, so the time increases by a factor of \(6/3=2\).

methods.label: Compare the distance and speed factors
methods.explanation:
Travel time equals distance divided by speed. The new distance is \(300/50=6\) times the old distance, which would require six times the time at the old speed. Traveling three times as fast divides that time by three, so
\[
\frac{\text{new time}}{\text{old time}}=\frac{6}{3}=2.
\]
The new time was twice as much, choice B.
methods.levelReason: Only the distance-speed-time relationship and elementary multiplication and division are required.
